correctness.rationale: For n≥2 a rank-k 0–1 partial permutation is brought to diag(I_k,0_q) by isometries. Stabilizer invariance of the unique Euclidean projection to Birkhoff gives four block entries. The matched off-diagonal b≥0 is optimally zero; minimizing F(c)=kq(q+2)c²+(1-kc)² gives c=1/[n+q(q+1)], feasible, a=1-q/D and d=(q+2)/D. This proves the unique nearest doubly stochastic point and squared error q(q+2)/D for 0<k<n; k=0 gives J/n, k=n gives M. Ratios give strictly ordered shells; convexity of squared distance and uniqueness of zero among farthest vertices show zero is the sole farthest point even in the full convex polytope. Counts C(n,q)^2(n-q)! and saddle of ratio (n-q)/(q+1)^2 yield CLT with variance 1/2, then delta method variance 1/8; checks do not replace saddle control.

value.rationale: Completing partial matchings to perfect fractional matchings is a natural Euclidean stability problem: the exact nearest matrix, all rank deficiency shells, and sharp q∼√n scale quantify a nontrivial geometric phase relation, and the unique continuous farthest point matters beyond enumerated vertices. Neither the rank count nor a generic projection method alone supplies this structural metric fact.

limitations: Projection formula applies only to partial-permutation vertices; continuous Hausdorff extremal statement applies to entire matching polytope.
